subject: Dedicated cutover: rightsize validation & runbook
messages:
From: Jason Wong <jason.wong@nebulasys.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@nebulasys.com>, Contracts <contracts@nebulasys.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated cutover: rightsize validation & runbook

Hi Monica —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We had a good internal sync and Nebula Systems is ready to move from the hosted API to a Dedicated fleet for our production traffic. Before we sign the reserved-capacity agreement we'd like to validate sizing and lock a cutover runbook with clear fallback windows.

Quick context:
- Current peak: ~420 req/sec (95th token length ~620 TL)
- Typical payload mix: 65% chat + 35% batch embedding calls
- SLA target: 99.9% availability, p95 latency <120ms for chat generations

Ask: can Redwood run a rightsize validation using our traffic profile and propose a 2-stage cutover (dry-run canary + production swap) with specific windows and rollback triggers? Also please attach any runbook template and the simulation inputs you need.

Attaching the Nebula traffic export (summary) in follow-up — I pulled the high-level CSV and contracts will start routing the SOW once we land sizing.

—Jason
Director of Platform
Nebula Systems
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Jason Wong <jason.wong@nebulasys.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@nebulasys.com>, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated cutover: rightsize validation & runbook

Jason — great, thanks for the context.

I pulled together a short validation plan and a runbook draft (attached: cutover-runbook-v1.pdf) and a sizing simulation workbook (rightsize-simulation-v2.xlsx). High level plan below — please confirm that this matches Nebula's expectations.

Planned approach:
1) Sizing validation (3 days): Redwood runs the simulation against the profile you shared, including mixed chat/embedding mix, token-length distribution, and arrival pattern. Deliverable: capacity matrix (instances / GPUs / expected QPS / p95 lat).
2) Dry-run (canary) — non-business-hour window: 2 hour window in which 10% traffic is routed to Dedicated; we will validate KV cache warmup, batching behavior, and cold-start characteristics. Success criteria: error rate <0.5%, p95 within 1.5x baseline.
3) Production cutover window: back-to-back 4 hour window with staged traffic increments (25% -> 60% -> 100%) and pre-defined rollback triggers.
4) Fallback plan: immediate automated routing back to hosted API if latency regressions exceed thresholds or if throughput falls below 80% of expected.

Questions for Nebula:
- Confirm preferred dry-run date window (we have engineers available Apr 7–9, but can move earlier if you need).
- Any datastore or private networking concerns for KV cache migrations?
- Is your security/compliance team comfortable with the cutover telemetry in the runbook (we include audit logs + request tracing)?

I've copied Karthik and Ben to validate the simulation assumptions on our side. Attaching runbook + sizing workbook now.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0132

Attachments: cutover-runbook-v1.pdf; rightsize-simulation-v2.xlsx
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Jason Wong <jason.wong@nebulasys.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 14:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated cutover: rightsize validation & runbook

Monica / Jason — quick note from the performance team after an initial pass on Nebula's numbers. I ran the traffic profile through the v2 workbook and a few preliminary observations:

- Baseline rightsize recommendation (best-effort): 12x A100-equivalent GPUs with mixed-instance packing (8 instances for chat-heavy tails, 4 for batch embeddings) to meet your p95 target at projected peak.
- For p95 headroom we recommend reserving 20% burst capacity (spot-backed) during the first 30 days of production cutover.
- KV cache warmup: expect 45–90 minutes for 80% warm cache hit rate under the observed prefix autocorrelation. We will run a targeted warmup during the canary.

Action items for Redwood engineers:
- I will schedule a simulated load run in our staging cluster (Apr 5) to validate the numbers; results to be shared by EOD Apr 5.
- Ben, can you confirm whether the proposed burst pool is acceptable from a cost and SL onboarding perspective?

Jason — could you share a P95-by-endpoint breakdown? That will let us refine the instance mix and batch / kernel tuning.

-Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Priya Rao <priya.rao@nebulasys.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Jason Wong <jason.wong@nebulasys.com>, Contracts <contracts@nebulasys.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 08:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated cutover: rightsize validation & runbook

Thanks — confirming a few items from Nebula side:

- Dry-run window: Apr 8, 03:00–05:00 PT (overnight for our US infra team) — confirmed.
- We attached the endpoint p95 breakdown and a short IAM network diagram in this reply (attached: nebula-p95-by-endpoint.csv; nebula-network-diagram.png).
- On burst pool: procurement prefers a clear stop-gap billing cap for burst GPU usage during the first 30 days — please include an estimate in the sizing workbook so we can sign off on the SOW.

One note on data flow: our compliance team needs assurance that request-level logs used for validation are hashed/anonymized before retention. Is that part of Redwood's standard cutover telemetry?

We'll route SOW/PO paperwork once sizing + cutover windows are agreed.

--Priya Rao
VP Product Ops, Nebula Systems
Contracts: contracts@nebulasys.com

Attachments: nebula-p95-by-endpoint.csv; nebula-network-diagram.png
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Priya Rao <priya.rao@nebulasys.com>, Jason Wong <jason.wong@nebulasys.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated cutover: rightsize validation & runbook

Priya / Jason — great, thanks for the fast responses and the endpoint breakdown. Summary / agreed next steps below:

1) Redwood will run the staging simulation on Apr 5 (karthik) and share the detailed capacity matrix by EOD Apr 5. (deliverable: rightsize matrix + burst estimate)
2) Dry-run (canary) scheduled Apr 8 03:00–05:00 PT. Redwood will perform KV warmup starting 01:30 PT and validate telemetry anonymization flows.
3) Production cutover tentative window Apr 12 01:00–05:00 PT — staged ramp 25%/60%/100% with rollback criteria defined in the attached runbook.
4) Contracts: monica will work with Nebula procurement on the SOW and include a billing cap for burst GPUs for the first 30 days. Please expect a DocuSign SOW link by Apr 6.

Telemetry / compliance: yes — anonymization/hashing of request bodies is standard for cutover validation; we will provide a scrubbing config and sample logs for Nebula to review prior to the dry-run.

Ben / Laura: please validate the SLA ladder language in sla-fallback-ladder.docx and confirm the DocuSign template (I will route).

If there are no objections I will mark the plan as confirmed and calendar the Milestone packet.

Thanks all — looking forward to the dry-run.

Monica Patel
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Monica.patel@redwood.com | (415) 555-0132

Attachments: sla-fallback-ladder.docx; cutover-runbook-v1.pdf; rightsize-simulation-v2.xlsx
